principles: Do not optimize for the sake of optimization.
Only address real correctness issues or define how to prove/disprove them.
Keep host-neutral and non-authority boundaries explicit.
Preserve logical consistency with existing Layer2 unlock and Authority receipt decisions.
drivers: F-009 is high severity and affects whether Layer2 Engineering PASS can be legitimately claimed.
The user asked for an executable document before implementation.
Existing docs already define much of the Layer2 proof contract, so the new doc should bridge the suspected gap instead of inventing a new layer.

options.name: A: Write a narrow F-009 execution plan document
pros: Directly addresses the open suspected finding.
Keeps proof, Authority, and claim boundaries explicit.
Avoids unlocking any capability from prose alone.
cons: Requires a later execution story before F-009 can be closed.

options.name: B: Immediately implement a proof producer/import path
pros: Could resolve F-009 faster if the finding is already verified.
cons: Risks arbitrary optimization before mechanical reproduction/disproof.
Could blur local CLI non-authority boundaries.

options.name: C: Treat F-009 as advisory and leave it for later
cons: Leaves a high suspected claim-gating gap without an executable handling path.
Does not satisfy the user request for a concrete execution document.

chosen: A: Write a narrow F-009 execution plan document
rationale: Option A matches the user request and the four principles: it creates the exact execution path for F-009 without prematurely implementing or claiming Layer2 unlock. It also preserves host-neutrality by using Claude and Codex as independent drafting hosts while the main auditor owns final consistency.

preMortem.scenario: Document accidentally claims Layer2 is unlocked.
preMortem.trigger: Language says PASS/unlocked instead of plan-only or future execution criteria.
preMortem.consequence: False capability claim and contradiction with F-009.
preMortem.mitigation: Add explicit non-goals and final audit checks for no unlock language.

preMortem.scenario: Document invents a new baseline layer or broad architecture.
preMortem.trigger: Host drafts suggest extra abstractions unrelated to F-009.
preMortem.consequence: Optimization for optimization and future maintenance burden.
preMortem.mitigation: Synthesize only correctness requirements needed to resolve/disprove F-009.

preMortem.scenario: Document treats local CLI as Authority server.
preMortem.trigger: Plan allows local commands to mint production receipts or production DONE.
preMortem.consequence: Violates Lattice CLI non-authority and host-neutral trust boundaries.
preMortem.mitigation: State local CLI can verify shape/import/gate consumption only; production receipt verification remains Authority-backed.
